text: There is also, as some of the Members alluded to, Mr Vikram Nair alluded to an asymmetry of costs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: You remember the situation that is going on now, it is called the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, this is what connects the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, where the Houthis fired drones.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The challenge is currently a focus of intense efforts everywhere, everyone is trying to find a cost-effective solution to the problem of mass small drones used for attack.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim spoke about how technology can disrupt militaries, and he is right.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, therefore, we must maintain our technological superiority, which includes the potential use of AI.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF and the SAF needs to partner this, and I agree with the MPs who have spoken about this, that we need to partner with civilian entities and use appropriate crowdsourcing.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, for example, MINDEF’s Future Systems and Technology Directorate and the DSO National Laboratories have launched the AI Grand Challenge, in partnership with AI Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The AI Grand Challenge has awarded funding to five teams to carry out research.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The theme was “Robust AI” or “AI for Materials Discovery”.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, the idea is that, over time, the SAF can harvest good ideas for its needs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And in fact, quite a number of emerging technologies are dual use, both civilian and military, with very quick adaptation cycles.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, for example, in the Russia-Ukraine war, an AI company was able to modify its commercial voice transcription to intercept Russia communications and automatically highlight key information to the Ukrainian armed forces.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: To capitalise on such opportunities, the SAF has set up technology adaptation teams.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Basically, you put combatants and engineers together, and their task is to adapt new technologies to the problems on the ground in quick and real time.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And we actually tested these teams during the recent Exercise Wallaby.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They had a practical problem where they needed to extend the range of communications, which they did by using a UAV fitted with a 5G base station to extend communications.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: All these new capabilities and structures will better prepare the SAF to defend Singapore, but it will come to nought if our soldiers are not committed or trained for their tasks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This was a recurrent theme by Mr Alex Yam, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Ms Poh Li San, and I agree with them.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF indeed has put significant amounts of money to invest in training infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Some of the Members wanted an update, so let me do that now.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAFTI City Phase 1 has been available for training since October last year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Battalions are trained in urban operations and homeland security, and the initial feedback has been very positive.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our SAF soldiers can feel the difference immediately.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The urban environment feels real, like stepping into an actual city.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Moving and driving through tight alleyways, clearing high-rise buildings and adapting to different scenarios pushes us to think fast and stay sharp.” It is gratifying because his reaction is exactly what we build SAFTI City for.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will build more of such facilities, and I think some Members wanted to know what more we can do, so that we can enhance realism for effective training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Pulau Tekong will be expanded to stretch 10 kilometres in distance.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We know 10 kilometres is not a huge stretch, but for Pulau Tekong, it is.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And we will find some way of stretching it so that you can make longer circuits.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, it will act as the Army’s second manoeuvre training area for soldiers as well as combat vehicles, because that is important as the Army becomes increasingly platform-based.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As Mr Chong Kee Hiong alluded to, it is overseas where we need to leverage large training spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And the Shoalwater Bay Training Area has been expanded with many new and better facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As a result of the expansion over the years, we were able to conduct the largest edition of Exercise Wallaby ever last year – over 6,200 personnel and 490 platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In Singapore, I can have 6,000 soldiers and 500 platforms but that is about it.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They will not have much room to move if you gather them together.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And they were tested to the limits, with the realism, because they were free to manoeuvre armour and armoured infantry, and the soldiers can feel it.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In the steady state, we are going to do more.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We thank the government and people of Australia for these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We look forward to commemorating the 10th anniversary of Singapore’s Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) with Australia this year and to explore further ambitious and strategic areas of cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Apart from infrastructure, we are doing more to recognise the contributions of our servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How and Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad will talk about this.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: There will be a new SAFRA Clubhouse in Bayshore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These investments to build our defence capabilities must be treated as precious resources.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is sizeable but it reflects a catch-up of projects deferred or disrupted due to COVID-19, we are still catching up, including those impacted by supply chain disruptions in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But going forward – the last three years we have been playing catch up – we expect smaller increases year-on-year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But given the rapid changes in our external environment, I think, we will have to continually monitor the situation closely and if the need arises, we must be prepared to invest more in further strengthening our capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Miss Rachel Ong, Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Henry Kwek talked about us needing to be self-reliant and at the same time, expanding our network of friends and partners where interests align.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As geopolitics becomes more unpredictable, it will affect our state-to-state relations with other countries, and that will also impact defence capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF takes reference from our overall foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Some partnerships are historical, like the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA).

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: There is a strong ongoing commitment from all partners.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The UK’s Prime Minister has announced that the UK Carrier Strike Group will be deployed to this region this year to take part in the FPDA exercise.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With Indonesia, the Defence Cooperation Agreement (DCA) has been in force, some Members wanted updates, let me give them now.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With Indonesia, the DCA has been in force since March last year and it provides a strong basis for us to promote closer interactions between our defence establishments, especially in new areas of defence cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our two leaders met in November 2024, Prime Minister Wong and President Prabowo, and both expressed support for more military engagement between the Tentara Nasional Indonesia (TNI) and the SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: President Prabowo invited the SAF to train in Indonesia, particularly Kalimantan, to train with the TNI and we will be taking up their offer as well as the joint air training.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Malaysia is at the helm of ASEAN this year and we will support their chairmanship as they uphold ASEAN centrality and unity.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, at the recent ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) Retreat, Singapore and Thailand introduced the protection of critical underwater infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Some MPs talked about this, whether it is energy grids or communications, that if they are disrupted, it affects nations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore and Thailand introduced a paper, Malaysia, as Chairman, strongly endorsed it and for the full concept paper to be formally tabled.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They continue to grow and we enjoy regular high-level exchanges with both countries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: On China, I co-chaired the Singapore-China Defence Ministers' Dialogue, this was in May last year and I did it on the sidelines of the Shangri-La Dialogue with then-recently appointed China Minister of National Defense Admiral (ADM) Dong Jun.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In September last year, I was invited to speak at their 11th Beijing Xiangshan Forum and also had a dialogue session, this was alongside, it was not part of the Xiangshan Forum, but we organised a dialogue session with their senior People's Liberation Army (PLA) commanders in their National Defence University (NDU) – the pinnacle group.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I also had a bilateral call with Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission GEN Zhang Youxia.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For those of you who know the PLA structure, it is a privilege, and my delegation and I acknowledge and appreciate the privileged access to both Vice Chairman Zhang and the pinnacle commander class at their NDU.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: During these meetings, we affirmed the good military-to-military interactions that we have through various exercises and these high-level meetings and we plan to step-up further interactions.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The US is a Major Security Cooperation Partner, our collaborations with their Department of Defense and military are extensive.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We are not a treaty ally, but it is plain that our military engagements and mutual benefits have grown over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore is thankful that our pilots have trained in the US for many years since the early 1970s.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: All our high-end fighting air platforms – the F-16s, F-15s, and soon F-35s – are manufactured by and purchased from US companies, alongside other high-end weapon platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore invests heavily into our own defence, and the US appreciates this fact.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The US also has a lead in dual-use technology that Singapore can benefit from.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Under former US Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin, our two Ministries signed new agreements to strengthen cooperation in defence innovation, in data, analytics and AI.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I look forward to further strengthening our defence relations under the Trump Administration.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Members in this House may remember that the Protocol of Amendment for the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the US was signed by President Trump and then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in 2019, during President Trump's first term.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This MOU bears some detailing, because it is important.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This MOU, I said that in 2019 it was a Protocol of Amendment, so the primary MOU, which was signed in 1990 by our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew and then-US Vice President Dan Quayle.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is important to know about this because it remains a cornerstone document for our military ties and engagements, wherein we facilitate rotations of US ships and planes through our military bases in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This 1990 MOU continues to underpin Singapore-US defence relations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: During my call with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, it occurred very soon after his confirmation, we both reiterated and affirmed our commitment to this long-standing defence relationship which has benefited both Singapore and US.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Secretary Hegseth was very familiar with the details of our past and present military engagements.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We also discussed further projects briefly and I invited him to the Shangri-La Dialogue and look forward to deepening our defence relations together.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As our defence capabilities grow, the SAF can do its part to help internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF's Changi Regional Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Coordination Centre (RHCC) works closely with both governmental and non-governmental organisations for humanitarian assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In September again, it also coordinated the delivery of aid supplies to communities affected by Typhoon Yagi in Lao PDR, Myanmar, and Vietnam.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Earlier this month, the RHCC worked on similar efforts to deliver another tranche of relief supplies to Gaza through Jordan using our MRTT.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This was to alleviate the humanitarian situation during the lead-up to Ramadan.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The SAF is making concrete plans to provide further medical assistance to the people in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have spoken to our counterparts in the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is not safe now to deploy SAF medical facilities in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The risks are high and unlikely to subside for some time to come.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We do not want to put SAF soldiers and civilian volunteers in harm's way there.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Apart from natural causes, chemical, biological, radiological and explosive (CBRE) threats can precipitate national and humanitarian crises.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We all saw this during SARS and COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: By extension, we should also realise that bioterrorism is a real threat.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF/SAF established the Network of ASEAN CBR Defence Experts when we were ADMM and ADMM-Plus Chair in 2018 to deal with this threat.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We conducted table-top exercises, training workshops, lab visits and created a harmonised set of guidelines to sample and analyse and to report.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We think it is time now to build a physical centre and this will greatly facilitate cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, that is what we are going to do.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We will work alongside RHCC, partner civilian agencies and military agencies across ASEAN and international organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I also announced in 2021, that MINDEF/SAF will build a Biosafety Level-4 lab.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: That MCF will provide us with the capability to assess the nature of an outbreak, isolate, identify the bioagent, and develop early disease control measures.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Just imagine if the equivalent of a Grade 4 bioagent was used and you are testing it in a Biosafety Lab 3.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It risks everyone being contaminated and you will not be able to test it.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So that BSL4 facility, I think, will strengthen our capabilities against bioterrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Mr Chairman, as the World around us becomes more unpredictable and changes, the more we need to keep the strongest commitment to strengthen our own defences and, if needed, we must be willing to do more.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore celebrates 60 years of Independence this year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: With the support of Members of this House, we will continue to build a strong SAF, to protect Singapore and keep Singapore as a sovereign and independent nation, and to ensure our peace and prosperity for another generation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: My Senior Ministers of State, my colleagues, will continue to answer the rest of your questions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, Defence Minister Dr Ng Eng Hen described our geopolitical environment as being marked by heightened tensions in recent years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Across generations, our NSmen's dedication has ensured that Singapore remains ready to face an increasingly complex security environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We do not take for granted the strong support for NS that we have.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Today, I will outline ongoing efforts to further strengthen NS and highlight new initiatives to enhance its effectiveness and to recognise our NSmen's contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Mr Mohd Fahmi asked how we are ensuring NSmen are deployed safely to meaningful operational roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The new system will assess each serviceman on a more granular scale, allowing better characterisation of their medical fitness and functional capacity so that they can be better matched to more operationally effective roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is a fundamental change that we are carefully studying and determining how to implement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over the past two years, we have been conducting functional assessments for pre-enlistees with selected orthopaedic conditions, in addition to the standard medical screening.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is heartening because it opens up more deployment options for our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It also allows the country as a whole to make best use of as many of our servicemen as possible in the defence of this nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF has also continued to leverage technology and redesign jobs to expand deployment opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Fahmi asked for an update on how we are continuously investing in the skills of our servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since 2018, we have partnered Institutes of Higher Learning on Work-Learn Schemes that allow Full-time NSFs to attain diplomas or partial university credits, while serving for a duration of three to four years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This enables NSFs to fulfil their academic aspirations and contribute meaningfully to the SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Since its inception, over 650 NSFs have enrolled in nine Work-Learn Schemes, serving in roles, such as Cyber Specialists, Air Force Technicians and Naval Warfare Systems Specialists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are also looking upstream to tap on the potential of pre-enlistees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, we introduced new schemes for polytechnic students to enlist and serve in the SAF while fulfilling their final-year internship requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We opened it to students in aerospace electronics, cybersecurity, electrical and electronic engineering and information technology courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Most recently, we partnered Temasek Polytechnic on the SAF-Polytechnic Sponsorship for Naval Warfare System Experts, where those selected will serve five years, fulfilling their polytechnic internship requirements, while picking up relevant skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The take-up rate for these schemes have been promising and this will be expanded to other polytechnics and vocations in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked for an update on how we are tapping on the rich skills and expertise of our Operationally Ready NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: One example is ME4(A) He Jianyuan who had served in the Air Force during his full-time NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: He was redeployed as an Assistant Engineering Officer in the Navy in view of his civilian expertise, leveraging a decade's worth of his marine engineering knowledge to assist the Chief Engineering Officer in mechanical and engineering operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about our efforts to improve the operational effectiveness of our Servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We have been attaching SAF medics to the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) under a collaborative programme which allows them to respond to critical incidents, gain hands-on experience and contribute to saving lives in high-pressure emergency situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, Lance Corporal (LCP) Chen Anhong was attached to the SCDF's paramedic team at Alexandra Fire Station for six months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: During the attachment, he responded to emergency calls daily, including a traffic accident with multiple casualties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As a first responder, LCP Chen administered life-saving treatment to casualties before they were conveyed to the hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This will alleviate the challenges faced by a lean ambulance crew, consequently resulting in enhanced patient care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSFs in the Island Defence Task Force will also be equipped with non-lethal pepper-spray projectile guns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This avails a more calibrated response to manage security incidents for better operational outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Maintaining operational effectiveness is crucial and this does not always come easy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: With respect to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's question on aircraft noise, MINDEF had previously shared with Members how local flight training is critical to our pilots' continued proficiency and operational readiness, and the measures RSAF has taken to reduce public inconveniences arising from aircraft noise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, where possible, local flying is conducted over waters rather than land and avoids residential areas during take-off, landing and transit to-and-from training areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The RSAF also flies at higher altitudes and lower airspeeds over land, to minimise noise to housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The Air Force also adjusts its training tempo during selected periods, such as the national exams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And this is over and above the training that we conduct overseas, which obviously does not result in noise over Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: While we are aware of experimental noise-reducing aerospace technology, such as fin-lined nozzles, engine insulation and aircraft fuselage shaping, there are, to our knowledge, currently no aircraft manufacturers that have certified or successfully incorporated the use of these technologies in the manufacturing of military aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Our Air Force will continue to monitor the development of such technologies and whether any can meet the operational requirements in a cost-effective way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: So, I want to reassure Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that we are doing our best in order to ensure that we can defend our skies, protect our country and, at the same time, minimise the inconvenience to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I spoke earlier about the initiatives to strengthen NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Now, I would like to elaborate on how upholding a strong safety culture in the SAF remains a priority, which is something that Mr Patrick Tay asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, arising from IGO's focus on driving safety, we designed "safe-to-fail" driving circuits that allow our transport operators to experience driving transgressions safely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Such circuits, coupled with driver monitoring systems installed in all SAF vehicles, have enabled us to correct improper driving habits and to ensure safer driving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Likewise, NSmen training now incorporates safety sharing and incident reporting in both the planning stages and debriefs, reflecting greater emphasis on safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We are confident that the ERPSS, like in previous panels, will offer valuable insights to shape improvements in our safety systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked how technology is used to improve training safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To sustain this strong safety culture, SAF has leveraged digitalisation to provide insights into safety performance, allowing safety efforts to be more targeted and more effective in accident prevention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will build on the foundation of the SAF's Enterprise Safety Information System, which is a platform for Servicemen to submit safety reports and access safety operating manuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The system will be upgraded with AI-enabled business processes and personalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond training safety, the psychological well-being of our Servicemen is just as important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Wan Rizal asked for an update.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Between 2020 and 2022, Care Hubs were set up in Basic Military Training (BMT) Centres to support NSFs during their transition to NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To sustain the delivery of care, we piloted the deployment of Roving Care Teams last year, and these teams comprised psychologists and counsellors, to partner unit commanders to enhance the immediacy of care for Servicemen after BMT.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In 2024, our Mental Health Office's well-being campaign focused on fostering a positive workplace culture across MINDEF/SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A new mental health e-learning module was launched to equip Servicemen with the knowledge and skills to build a positive workplace culture and offer peer support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The SAF is also applying evidence-based best practices to strengthen psychological resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: AReC has implemented these in BMT, and we have seen higher training participation and Servicemen reporting improved ability to cope with challenging tasks during military training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Apart from enhancing NSmen's operational effectiveness and sustaining a strong safety culture, we also want to improve the NS experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will do more to facilitate the enlistment process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF is collaborating with GovTech and the Public Service Division to incorporate pre-enlistment features on the LifeSG app to complement existing MINDEF touchpoints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This year, we will progressively roll out personalised features on the app to pre-enlistees commencing NS registration, when they turn 16 and a half years old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This includes push notifications to provide timely reminders on key tasks, and a milestone tracker which tracks their progress from NS registration to enlistment, providing information, such as their Physical Employment Standard (PES) status as well as enlistment dates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Members who are NSmen would also be familiar with the OneNS app and web portal released last April.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about the enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen can now access NS digital services with fewer disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen can submit applications for deferment of In-Camp Trainings (ICT) on the platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The OneNS Portal is constantly enhanced to address feedback from Servicemen through surveys submitted after their NS activities in order to improve the user experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We will continue to enhance OneNS, so that Servicemen can access their ICT records on-the-go and utilise their NS credits more conveniently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Ms Jean See asked for updates about the new Central Manpower Base (CMPB).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, I shared with Members that the new CMPB was under construction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This new CMPB, located opposite Cashew Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station, will be an integrated one-stop service centre consolidating Servicemen's various NS administrative needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This includes completing medical screenings, attending NS fitness activities at the all-weather Fitness Conditioning Centre, as well as purchasing NS necessities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The new CMPB will also house the second Regional Health Hub (RHH), which will span two levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: And that RHH will consolidate key healthcare facilities into one location.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Today, a pre-enlistee with pre-existing medical conditions will have to visit multiple locations on different days for his medical classification test and specialist reviews.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: At RHH, which will come up at the new CMPB, this pre-enlistee will be able to complete his medical assessments in a single visit, with specialist appointments scheduled on the same day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: An improved queue management system will also reduce waiting times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: By streamlining these medical processes, the hub is expected to serve around 200 Servicemen daily, ensuring prompt and comprehensive healthcare support throughout their NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond consolidating NS-related administrative needs, the new CMPB also functions as a community space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The public can access exercise facilities, such as an outdoor running path, fitness zone and even a soccer field.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Residents who live nearby will have access to amenities, such as a childcare centre, a café and a food court that will operate even in the evenings and on weekends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I have covered how MINDEF/SAF will continue to enhance the NS experience and would like to wrap up my speech by underlining our efforts to recognise our Servicemen's contributions to the defence and security of Singapore, which Ms Denise Phua asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Members will recall that in November last year, MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) disbursed $200 worth of NS LifeSG credits to 1.2 million past and present NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These credits can be used for a variety of essential goods and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Over 77% of eligible NSmen have made at least one transaction using their NS LifeSG credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: I am glad that our NSmen have found these credits helpful.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Gerald Giam shared his views on how NS should be value-accretive and suggested some ways to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: As I shared with Members last year, we fully recognise and value our NSFs' contributions to the defence of this country and for which there is an NS allowance which recognises those contributions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond recognition packages, each NSF receives a monthly allowance that supports his personal upkeep and recognises his service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We regularly review the NS allowances so that they remain adequate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The last adjustment was made in July 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This is an increase of about 4% to 5% for most NSFs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Another key effort in supporting our NSFs is to facilitate their transition to work and studies after completing NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This includes helping NSFs develop skills that can apply in their civilian life after NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: A study conducted by the Institute of Policy Studies in 2022 found that seven in 10 Singaporeans agreed that NS was beneficial for learning skills useful for civilian employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond practical skills, about nine in 10 agreed that NS was important for personal character development, such as instilling discipline and values, and transforming our NSFs from “boys to men”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how we have enhanced NSFs’ employability and supported their transition into the workforce and further education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Apart from the Certificate of Service package that documents the skills and competencies they gained during NS, the SAF also works with SkillsFuture Singapore to accredit certifiable skills under the national Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: For example, NSFs can receive accreditation for the skills they acquire through BMT and specialist courses, such as in leadership, medical and logistics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: In addition, since 2022, MINDEF and MHA have partnered the NTUC Learning Hub and the NTUC Employment and Employability Institute to enhance the SkillsFuture@NS programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: These are transferrable skills that NSFs can apply in their transition to work and studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We continue to encourage more of them to sign up to benefit from this resource.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Together, we will keep Singapore safe and secure for generations to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister for Defence Dr Ng briefly mentioned SAFRA Bayshore earlier in his speech, allow me to provide more details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SAFRA was set up in 1972 to recognise NSmen and build bonds among servicemen and their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I cannot emphasise enough the role that the families play in supporting our servicemen through their NS commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will have direct access to the MRT, which will provide greater convenience to users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Ng and Senior Minister of State Mr Heng also updated the House on our efforts to ensure that the SAF remains effective and ready to defend Singapore, and this is amidst a more challenging geopolitical environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must also be prepared for the risks of various kinds of disruptions caused by climate change, cyber-attacks or civil emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Many of these disruptions are not limited to the military domain but have impacts on the wider society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To answer Mr Saktiandi Supaat’s questions, the threat of such far-reaching disruptions is part of the reason why Total Defence, our concept of a whole-of-society defence, remains as relevant and useful today as it was in 1984, when we first started Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Looking back, some of the disruptions we face today – food, water, and power disruptions – are similar to those we faced back in 1984.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, as our lives became more interconnected and fast-paced, these disruptions have the potential to be more severe and more far-reaching than before.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Other sources of disruption are more recent, such as disruptions caused by cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, or extreme weather arising from climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have experienced some of these disruptions in the past, and we must be prepared for such disruptions in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The six pillars of Total Defence – military, economic, social, civil, digital and psychological – working in concert have allowed us to respond to different crises that jeopardised Singapore’s future over the past four decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These pillars provide us with a strong foundation for our defence and based on a public poll that we conducted last year, we are glad that most Singaporeans are willing to partner with us, to play their part in bringing Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, the same poll found that Singaporeans were less confident about our preparedness to withstand crises and disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As such, MINDEF/SAF has been working with Singaporeans to strengthen community resilience and readiness for disruptions, particularly though Exercise SG Ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Alex Yam and Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about Exercise SG Ready and MINDEF’s efforts in strengthening societal resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, we conducted the first Exercise SG Ready, to prepare Singaporeans for disruptions to food and water resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I reported last year that over 800 organisations participated in simulated disruptions of our water, our food and our power supplies, as well as cyber disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The positive response has rallied more organisations to come on board this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over 600 participating organisations also took the opportunity to exercise their business continuity plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, Senoko Energy simulated a total blackout of their power plant, where all its generators were shut down and restarted using back-up generators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Several multinational and local financial institutions also reviewed their readiness plans through a Table-Top Exercise organised by Quantedge Capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Close to 200 organisations also took part in a coordinated phishing exercise, of which half were small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year’s exercise was also unique in spotlighting the need to care for the vulnerable segments of society during major disruptions, as part of SG60.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, corporates like HP Inc. have adopted Active Ageing Centres to support seniors in times of crises, ensuring that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF also supported the Singapore Association for the Deaf in developing sign-language educational videos on emergency preparedness for the Deaf community, to ensure that they are aware and prepared for cyber or power disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Aside from disruptions caused by accidents or malicious actors, we also have to prepare for the risk of disruptions arising from climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Climate change is not just an existential threat for a low-lying island like Singapore, its effects are being felt today in the form of extreme weather events. 2024 was one of the hottest years on record, and in January, we felt the effects of climate change in the form of prolonged rain and flash floods because of the monsoon surge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To prepare our community for disruptions caused by such extreme weather, we conducted a community Table-Top Exercise with PUB in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The event brought together over 50 grassroots leaders, residents, youths and business representatives to discuss an extreme flooding scenario, and how to plan and prepare for such a scenario, in partnership with community groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to hold more of such exercises to increase our community preparedness and resilience, bringing together the experience of our community leaders, the experience of our business representatives and the energy of our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These exercises covered some of the likely disruptions that we may encounter in the coming years, and I am glad that many Singaporeans today are now more prepared to face these disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond preparing Singaporeans for disruptions caused by climate change, MINDEF/SAF is also part of the Singapore Government’s sustainability efforts to safeguard Singapore’s future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the past three years, we have been installing rooftop solar panels in all suitable SAF camps, as part of HDB’s Solar Nova programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: By the end of this year, we will have rooftop solar panels in most of our camps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The locations for these solar panels were carefully selected to ensure that our operational effectiveness would not be affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This included detailed studies to ensure that the glare from the solar panels would not pose a danger to military aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to expand solar deployment to other MINDEF/SAF camps and premises where operationally feasible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also on track to achieving our other sustainability targets, including a 10% reduction in water and energy utilisation and a 30% reduction in Waste Disposal Index.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, the RSAF has built a super low energy flight simulator in Tengah Airbase, which consumes up to 40% less energy than previous designs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Chinook wash shed, which uses up to 60% less water per wash this time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2024, the estimated amount of water saved was equivalent to the average daily amount of water used by about 1,500 four-room HDB flats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also implemented trials of the Smart Utilities Metering System at three SAF camps, with good results of up to 10% reduction in electricity consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will begin rolling them out in all SAF camps and bases in the next few years, which will further help us to maximise the resource efficiency of our buildings and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about how MINDEF is investing resources to contribute to sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through these initiatives, I would assure Members that MINDEF/SAF is committed to achieving our sustainability targets in line with the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, looking forward, it is pertinent that we continue to partner all Singaporeans to strengthen our collective commitment to Total Defence, so as to safeguard Singapore’s future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We need to continue to advocate for and engage Singaporeans on the need for Total Defence, to build a strong, secure and cohesive nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked for a summary of our initiatives last year to commemorate 40 years of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Aside from improving our community resilience through Exercise SG Ready, we also focused on inspiring Singaporeans to act and energising our Total Defence practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: From February to October last year, we conducted a Total Defence Exhibition at 52 locations around Singapore, where we showcased examples of Singaporeans putting Total Defence in action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also engaged and energised over 300 National Education and Total Defence practitioners through the inaugural Total Defence Convention, organised jointly with the National University of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Practitioners from Government agencies, educational institutions, community groups and businesses were able to come together to exchange best practices, network and discuss ideas around the theme of "Building Societal Resilience and Readiness in Crises and Disruptions".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, we will continue to engage specific groups to strengthen community resilience while engaging all Singaporeans to strengthen commitment to Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of the ways we will do this is through the Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence (ACCORD), which Miss Rachel Ong spoke about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: ACCORD runs a wide range of community outreach initiatives, bringing society together to champion and advocate for Singapore's defence and for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some MPs such as Mr Don Wee, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Neil Parekh and Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim are also active members of ACCORD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under the agreement, the SBF will conduct activities to engage businesses in support of Total Defence and national resilience and will conduct cybersecurity training and exercises for businesses to strengthen their digital defence and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since 2021, ACCORD has also been conducting virtual visits to the Basic Military Training Centre (BMTC) for Singaporean families residing overseas, ensuring that both pre-enlistees and their parents have greater access to NS information and feel more connected to the NS journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Miss Rachel Ong also asked about how we are encouraging and enabling conversations about Total Defence, especially with our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One way we do so is through our MOU with Temasek Foundation, which was recently renewed to provide cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and automated external defibrillator (AED) training as well as psychological first aid certification training for all nine uniformed groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will extend this initiative for an additional year to continue equipping cadets from uniformed groups with valuable knowledge to identify and respond effectively to medical emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Such initiatives strengthen our community resilience and our readiness for crises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also want to continue strengthening our engagement of Singaporeans through presenting our defence stories and messages in new and exciting ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked for an update on our MINDEF/SAF museums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last August, our Singapore Air Force Museum was handed over to Defence Collective Singapore to operate alongside the Singapore Discovery Centre and Singapore Navy Museum.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Singapore Air Force Museum will undergo a refresh this year to update its galleries and introduce more engaging and immersive programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond the fleet of aircraft on display, the refreshed museum will feature precious artefacts and equipment from the early days of the RSAF, telling the story of the growth and innovation of our Air Force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Looking further ahead, we can look forward to the re-opening of the Army Museum of Singapore in Jurong in 2027 after it completes a major revamp and the opening of the NS Gallery in 2028.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These refreshed museums will inspire visitors to defend what it means to be Singaporean.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is part of our overall effort to explore new and innovative ways to expand our reach and put Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This brings me to my last point – encouraging innovation in support of Total Defence, which Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For the past three years, I have mentioned the Total Defence Sandbox as our flagship initiative to call for and implement ideas from Singaporeans on how the community can put Total Defence in action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, I would like to highlight the Total Defence-themed hackathon YouthxHack as an initiative that empowers our youth to put Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The four-day event organised by Cyber Youth Singapore last September involved over 160 participants across 36 teams coming up with innovative ideas to strengthen the digital, social and economic pillars of Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In response to the Hackathon's challenge to enable the public to distinguish between trustworthy and malicious interactions, one of our hackathon teams developed the "5Seconds" initiative to provide a secure and scalable communication method between businesses and customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The application enables convenient and secure communication over email and SMS through encryption, eliminating concerns over phishing and bolstering public trust in our digital communications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since the hackathon, the team behind "5Seconds" has participated in several events to showcase their solution, including at the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises' Artificial Intelligence Festival Asia event in January, sharing their solution to help improve the digital defence of our companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These are just some examples of the projects we have received from youths over the past year, which we are supporting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The active participation and creativity of our youth give me confidence that together, we can build a strong, secure and cohesive nation capable of dealing with any crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to close by reiterating that the world we live in is a challenging one and the threat of disruptions in the future is all but certain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF has been and will continue investing in Total Defence as our best preparation and our best response to these disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are doing our part towards meeting the sustainability targets as part of the Singapore Green Plan 2030 to safeguard our collective future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened that Singaporeans have also been preparing and equipping themselves and contributing in creative ways towards strengthening Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to partner Singaporeans in this shared responsibility of keeping Singapore strong for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am confident that together, we can build a strong, cohesive and secure Singapore for many generations to come.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I also thank the Minister for answering my questions on training safety.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I welcome the news that SAF and MOH will consider further medical assistance deployments to help civilians affected in Gaza.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: First of all, exactly last year, I was with Minister Vivian Balakrishnan in the Middle East.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: We saw the military humanitarian drop in Gaza, but I must say I was quite concerned about the safety of our troops.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: The Minister mentioned how it is not safe right now to establish medical facilities in Gaza, but they are thinking of deploying in safe areas in the region in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Of course, the safety of our troops is of utmost importance and mission success critical.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Regarding details – when and the size of it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Usually, the process is that we will evaluate sending a needs assessment team.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy accompanied the SAF Multi-Role Tanker Transport (MRTT), there was a recent delivery of aid.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Subsequently, they went from there to meet some counterparts in Egypt for fact finding.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But in response to the Member's question, ultimately, what we deploy, we want it to be meaningful.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There will have to be, of course, a medical element.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When I mentioned MOH, it is in the context of MOH also has a volunteer programme.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If they could be co-deployed, we will look for opportunities there.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In addition, there was to be security, logistics.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I do not want to give numbers now because we are not there yet.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But usually, it is more than what we have deployed there.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But ultimately, we recognise that it is a humanitarian situation and we want to give medical assistance, and we think the SAF can contribute.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The truth is, it will help, but I will not stance the mission for that.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is primarily a humanitarian assistance and disaster relief mission.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think the Minister mentioned that in relation to drones, the Air Force is going to have a special unit dealing with it.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The Army will have a drone accelerator as well.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Are there any plans for the Navy to similarly have its own unit dealing with unmanned technologies?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The second clarification is – in a world that is increasingly fracturing and alliances may become more uncertain, to what extent are we also doing acquisitions of defence technology locally and helping the local defence industry to grow?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Air Force and the Army initiatives to set up units to consolidate or path find for unmanned systems, I have explained.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Navy already, as I mentioned, deploys uncrewed platforms.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They are already in operations in the Singapore Strait.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Whether they need a dedicated unit, I leave it to them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is where I will just leave it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For procurement, obviously, foreign policy will affect our business dealings.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is often said, trade and security are two faces of the same coin.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But there are realities of our current procurement.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In terms of the platforms we need, we are always guided by effectiveness and, of course, cost.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the platform has to be effective, has to meet our security needs.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And we will buy the best in class.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Then, we will see where it is manufactured, the price and also the maintenance.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, as we did for our frigates.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think it is easier for naval platforms because we have got some experience and worked with partners.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But even then, certain modules may also have multinational involvement, but yes, it may be built here.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For the Army, as you can imagine, tanks may be a different class, but we could build the Titan, as we build other platforms.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For planes, it is a bit more difficult.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The planes that we purchase from US manufacturers are deemed to be at the front edge.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think for some time yet, they will continue to be seen as that.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: This would avoid a situation where defence spending spikes just because we have strong economic growth in a certain year or drops if the converse happens.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Lastly, I appreciate Senior Minister of State Heng's announcement that NS allowances will increase in July.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is going to be very hard to plan, because ex ante you do not know how the economy will do.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you ask dollars this year and we go into a COVID-19 pandemic as it did, that is not practical.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Or you ask X dollars based on last year's performance and you have conflict, so I am not sure that that system works.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As I said, our starting basis is that defence is a long-term investment business.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The starting point must be, not only for Singapore, but for all countries.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Actually what we have, is quite amazing, that you can actually start from that basis: what does the military need to secure Singapore's defences?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And for any country, that must be the starting basis.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Then you say, well, can I afford it and how long do I take to achieve that basis?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It cannot be pegged to the economic performance because it may not be related.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I do not think any serious planner would go on that and I would not suggest anybody does that.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: You start from the basis, what do I need to defend Singapore adequately and then, you say, well, what do I need?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But in practical terms, what is also constrained and is a virtuous state, because our economy has been growing and the Members of this House has supported the defence budget that we have asked for.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Our practical constraints have been not so much in dollars but in manpower.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For instance, if you had operated the previous artillery – remember you needed 12 people to stabilise the base plates and so on – and now, with shoot-and-scoot systems, you only need three people.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Or previous naval vessels, which required many more men, but were redesigned so that you require less.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think we try to keep this virtuous state of affairs as long as we can to make sure that we can invest steadily.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Year-to-year fluctuations would occur, whether it is economic, not so much in COVID-19, but remember the Global Financial Crisis?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you have to take a haircut, you have to take a haircut.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: MOF says, "This is what I have and you have to live within your means", and we will adjust.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But the relationship we have together with MOF is very useful, it is not from year to year, it is over a period.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And it allows MINDEF/SAF to make year to year adjustments, but at the same time keep to the overall schedule of building our SAF.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Giam for his question.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: However, I just wanted to emphasise two points.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: So, if you look at the entire journey, SAF and MINDEF does help to improve or invest in the retirement adequacy for our NSmen as well.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: More broadly, I think one should really see how the Government looks after Singaporeans and find different ways in which to help Singaporeans get a good education, to be able to access good jobs and then, to be able to earn and to save in a regular manner.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Taken together, we would want to ensure that a Singaporean who works consistently and pays into CPF during his work life, will have the ability to have basic retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: As an economist, I would like to ask a geopolitical and defence-related question in terms of threat assessment, whether the Minister can share whether Singapore can continue balancing US and China interests, especially within these geopolitical dynamics and what your defence outlook would be?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Mr Chairman, I encourage the Member to direct that question to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in terms of crafting our foreign policy, which will come after this.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I am sure there are many live questions.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Remember the famous line, "There are no permanent friends, there are only permanent interests".

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And that is true for our countries, as the interest change, as the global system change.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But what I have tried to explain is that we ourselves can be the slow frog that is being boiled.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We get socialised to things that are different and we say, "Well, that is just the norm".

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And if you think it is business as usual, you are in serious trouble.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And the question for us is, what is coming?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And the answer to that, as I was trying to explain in historical terms, you do not know.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: There was a famous quote which I like to use and this is from Secretary Robert Gates, and I respect him immensely, previous Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) director, serious mien; when you speak to him, you can see the machination in his brain going, the database going.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: You know he weighs his answers because there is a lot going on.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But he made this speech to West Point Cadets graduation.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He said and I paraphrase him that the US' record for predicting where they would go into military operations has been perfect.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Out of the last 10 military campaigns, they never got it right, 100% wrong.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And then he added and this is the clincher, "We never got it right even a year from deployment." Just think.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: US, with its vast intelligence; just as US before the Pearl Harbor attack, with its vast intelligence, with a vast machinery, cannot get it right one year before a conflict.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: If you think what you know what is coming, you tell me, you may be Nostradamus.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But I tell you, you can sense something is coming, you just do not know what it is.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But when you see machines spinning faster and faster, one will spin out of orbit and something will break.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: How do you prepare Singapore and Singaporeans for that kind of scenario?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is all fundamentals, because you really do not know what is coming.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I mean, we have to do our part.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I think as Singapore grows in capability and wealth, I think we need to do more, but we are not out there to deal with every humanitarian situations, where we find that there are needs and if we can contribute effectively, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I can cost it for you in terms of dollars – it is not cheap every time we send a military plane, but that is probably the wrong way of assessing it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: But we wanted to send a signal and these are the considerations.

speaker: The Chairman
text: On that note, Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Ng Eng Hen, Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How and Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad for sharing the good work of MINDEF and SAF in an increasingly uncertain world.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I would also like to thank all the staff at MINDEF and the people of SAF.
